title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes build an axiomatic 'analysis situs', a programme toward the 'topologie modérée' (tame topology) of the Esquisse. The primitives are the following.
- Figures F, G, X, ...
- A 'part-of' relation ≪ and a second order ≤.
- A dissociation relation ∥, meaning separated or disjoint. Its negation is written ∥̄.
- A class 𝓛 of elementary or atomic figures, which behave like connected strata or cells.
- A class 𝓜 of 'model' figures.
- For each figure F, a canonical decomposition omb(F) ⊂ 𝓛 into strata. The transcription sometimes reads this as 'amb'.
- For F' ≪ F and G ≪ F, a restriction F'_G with omb(F'_G) = omb(F') ∩ omb(G).

The page finishes the proof of the Lemma begun on p.82.
- Lemma. Let F' ≪ F, G ≪ F, F'_G ≪ G and H ≪ G. If H ∥ F'_G, then H ∥ F'.
- Proof strategy. It suffices to show x' ∥ x for every stratum x' ∈ omb F' and every stratum x ∈ omb H.
- If x' ∈ omb F'_G, this is the hypothesis.
- Otherwise, this page argues as follows. Since x'_G ≤ x' and x' is atomic (in 𝓛), we get x'_G = x' or x'_G = ∅. Since x' is not ≪ F'_G, x'_G = ∅. Hence x' ∈ omb(F) \ omb(G).
- A stratum x of H lies in omb(G) ⊂ omb(F). So x and x' are distinct strata of the decomposition omb(F). Axiom At 12 (distinct strata are mutually dissociated) then gives x ∥ x'.
- The Lemma serves p.82: replacing an initial definition by one that no longer needs an explicit witness stratum. It is applied with G = X and H = z.

New axiom At 13 ('quasi-existence of elements' / completeness). Let F ≪ X with X ∈ 𝓜. Suppose some nonempty figure G (which may be taken in 𝓛) satisfies G ∥ F and G ∥̄ X. Then some stratum x ∈ omb X satisfies x ∥ F, and automatically x ∥̄ X. The right margin groups At 8, At 9, 9E and At 13 as axioms guaranteeing the existence of 'many' elements. The idea is that the strata of a model are fine enough to witness any separation that exists at all.

Corollary. For F' ≪ F, the following are claimed equivalent:
- (i) every G dissociated from F' is dissociated from F;
- (ii) no stratum of F (written omb(X)) is dissociated from F';
- (iii), on p.84: F' is maximal among figures F̄' with F' ≤ F̄' ≪ F.

This is an intrinsic notion of 'F' dense / essential in F', characterised separation-theoretically, stratum-wise, and order-theoretically. Page 84 proves (i)⇔(ii) via At 13 and (ii)⇔(iii) via the join F' ∨ x. It then asks whether these imply a ≪-maximality condition (iv).
errors: In Corollary (ii) the quantifier is over omb(X), but no X is in context; it should be omb(F) (or F should be the X ∈ 𝓜 of At 13).
The step 'x'_G ≤ x' with x' ∈ 𝓛 ⇒ x'_G = x' or ∅' silently uses an atomicity property of 𝓛 under restriction, which must be one of the earlier axioms.
Concluding x ∥ x' needs x ≠ x' as strata of omb(F). This follows from x ∈ omb(G) and x' ∉ omb(G), but it presupposes omb(H) ⊂ omb(G) ⊂ omb(F); compatibility of the stratifications is implicit.
The variable names x/y and x'/y' are used inconsistently between p.82 and p.83.

ideas.what: Lemma: dissociation from a sub-figure can be tested on its restriction to an ambient piece, proved stratum by stratum using the atomicity of strata and the dissociation of distinct strata
ideas.modern_name: disjointness in a stratification / cell decomposition (strata of a common refinement are pairwise disjoint)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Łojasiewicz); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries)

ideas.what: Axiom At 13: if a model figure X has some nonempty piece separated from F and not separated from X, then some stratum of X is separated from F (existence of enough elements)
ideas.modern_name: an atomicity / enough-points axiom, akin to atomic Boolean contact algebras in mereotopology, or to 'enough points' for a site
ideas.usually_credited_to: mereotopology (Whitehead, de Laguna; Düntsch–Winter contact algebras); enough points (SGA4)

ideas.what: Corollary characterising when a subfigure F' ≪ F is 'dense': separation-wise (i), stratum-wise (ii), order-maximality (iii)
ideas.modern_name: density / essential subobject; regular-closed elements in contact algebras

ideas.what: Global programme: a point-free axiomatic of tame topology based on figures, part-of, dissociation and atomic strata
ideas.modern_name: tame topology / o-minimality; point-free topology / mereotopology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984, programme only); van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (o-minimality)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 states the programme of 'topologie modérée' but not this axiomatic

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics (figures, ≪ = part-of, ∥ = dissociation, atomic strata in 𝓛, existence axioms At 8/9/13) is in substance a stratified mereotopology, close to (atomic) Boolean contact algebras and region-based theories of space. The two literatures, Grothendieck's tame-topology programme and mereotopology / point-free contact structures, have not been connected.
missed.quote: NB At 8, At 9, 9 E), At 13 sont des axiomes d'existence de "beaucoup" d'éléments
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give a point-free, mereotopological axiomatisation of o-minimal or tame geometry, linking contact-algebra representation theorems with o-minimal cell decomposition.

missed.claim: Whether the density conditions (i)-(iii) imply ≪-maximality (iv) is left open on the next page; the system of axioms At 1–At 13 is never completed into a published theory.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is part of an unpublished axiomatic tame topology. Its completeness relative to o-minimal structures is untested.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly a routine lemma within a private axiom system. Mildly notable is the explicit formulation of an 'existence of enough strata' axiom inside a point-free, dissociation-based axiomatic of tame topology. This is an undocumented facet of Grothendieck's 1986 analysis situs and closely parallels mereotopology.
transcription_corrections: 'amb(F)', 'amb(G)', 'amb X', 'amb(X)' are most likely 'omb' throughout (same symbol as on p.82).
'$x'_G = x'$ ou' — the first equation reads x'_G = x' (the image shows a primed x).
The final At reference reads 'At 12' (reasonably legible).
In At 13, the inserted words are '(on)' before 'G ∥ F' and 'qu'on' before 'pourra'; '(NB on sait qu'on pourra alors prendre G ∈ 𝓛)'.
Right margin: 'NB At 8, At 9, 9E), At 13 sont des axiomes d'existence de "beaucoup" d'éléments' — the transcription is essentially right.
Left margin is largely illegible; it seems to name At 13 an 'Axiome de ... d'existence' (possibly 'de quasi-existence d'éléments' or 'de complétude'), with a reference to (𝓜, 𝓛).
